result.best:
The recommended combination is forward differences in every refinement of the search, no intermediate covariance, the returned fit refined once more with central differences (its covariance from that pass), held frames de-duplicated by canonical(), and only the class's distinct low-index starts (no random fill). That gives 7 starts in m−3 and m−3m, 9 in −3m, 6/m and 6/mmm, and 11 as today in the other six classes.

Full 77-run screening set, against today's run in the pilot:
- **Evaluations:** 151 381 against 307 235 (0.493×; median per run 0.497). The parts: forward differences + no covariance 0.525×; central pass +0.006×; held dedupe −0.007×; symmetric starts −0.031×.
- **Search time:** 43.1 s against 76.9 s a run, so 55.3 against 98.7 min summed. result.why:
**Where the evaluations go.** Today's search spends 60 % of its evaluations in the 11 briefs (8 iterations each, about 220 evaluations), 23 % in the 3 full refinements, about 10 % in the held frames, and the rest in polish, exact and refit. An iteration is a Jacobian (2 evaluations per non-linear column, central) plus about 1.2 trial steps. Every refinement also ended with a covariance: 1 + 2 evaluations per non-linear parameter, about 10 % of a brief.

**(1) No intermediate covariance.** The covariance is made after convergence and only the returned fit's is read. Dropping it cannot change any step: 0.908× evaluations and identical minima on 22/22 runs.

**(2) Forward differences.** They halve each Jacobian.
- The iteration counts did not change at the median (brief 7.9, full 11.4 against 11.5), and the minima were today's on 22/22 runs.
- Where the path diverged, the fit ended at the same χ² (cylinder-P4mmm-on: 45 against 32 full iterations).
- The ratio by class is 0.49–0.58. It is highest in 4/mmm and m−3, where trial steps and audits weigh more in a run.

**Why wall time falls less than evaluations.** 96–98 % of the search's time is in pattern evaluations. An evaluation outside a Jacobian (trial step, FCJ audit, covariance) costs 1.5–2.5× a Jacobian column: 20.1 against 13.5 ms, 48.6 against 19.5 ms. Forward differences halve only the cheap Jacobian evaluations, so the dear ones become a larger share (16 % → 27 %) and the mean cost per evaluation rises by 10–20 %. The likely cause is caches the engine keeps when only one parameter moves; this was inferred, not traced.

**The central pass.** On a forward-difference minimum it costs 1 iteration (44 evaluations median) and moves χ² by 0.0003 χ²_ν median: the forward and central minima are the same point. Its few moves (at most 0.61 χ²_ν, 4.5 % in an extent, 1.7° in an axis) are all free fits in flat valleys, where the shift test had stopped. Its marginal cost over the covariance it replaces is 24 evaluations a run.

**(3) Held frames.**
- The refinement is equivariant under the class's rotations, so equivalent frames end at the same χ² in the same number of evaluations; skipping them changes nothing.
- They exist only where a rotation of the class maps one candidate frame onto another (in 4/m and above): 29 of 124 held refinements on the 77 runs, none in −1, 2/m or mmm.
- Because the held refinements are a small stage, the saving is small: 28 evaluations a run.

**(4) Symmetry and starts.**
- lowIndexAxes already gives one axis per Laue family, and a plate and a needle along one family are different starts, so no deterministic start is equivalent to another.
- The only symmetry redundancy is the random fill to 11. It exists only where the class has fewer than 5 low-index families: 2 random starts in −3m, 6/m and 6/mmm, 4 in cubic. That is how higher symmetry already lowers the number of distinct starts.
- Dropping the fill saves 15 % of the search in those five classes (36–52 % of today's evaluations there). It cost one free-fit miss of 2.6 χ²_ν beside an identical held result.
- Restricting the fill to the fundamental zone at 20° from every start gives no better reach and costs more than dropping it. A uniform random rotation is already uniform in the zone modulo symmetry, and the fill's random shapes found basins (44 in the pilot logs) whose minima the deterministic starts reached anyway in 24 of 27 runs.

**(4b) Full refinements from distinct brief ends.** The 3 best brief ends are often duplicates by an 8°/28 % test (52 of 77 runs). Dropping the duplicates looks safe on the pilot logs (69 of 78 ended alike) but costs reach on the 77, up to 191 χ²_ν on box-Pmmm-on. Briefs of 8 iterations are not converged, and ends that close can still lead to different minima.

result.best:

- forward differences in every refinement of the search, with no intermediate covariance;
- the returned fit refined once more with central differences, its covariance taken from that pass;
- held frames de-duplicated by canonical();
- only the class's distinct low-index starts (no random fill). That is 7 starts in m−3 and m−3m, 9 in −3m, 6/m and 6/mmm, and 11 as today in the other six classes.

In the engine the fill's random numbers can still be drawn and thrown away, as here, so that the polish and refit turns stay today's.

All figures below are on the full 77-run screening set, against today's run in the pilot (score.mjs --supersede; symA from the fixed stream).
- **Evaluations:** 151 007 against 307 235 (0.492×; median per run 0.499). By part: forward differences + no covariance 0.525×; central pass +0.006×; held dedupe −0.007×; symmetric starts −0.032×.

result.why:
**Where the evaluations go.** Today's search spends:
- 60 % of its evaluations in the 11 briefs (8 iterations each, about 220 evaluations);
- 23 % in the 3 full refinements;
- about 10 % in the held frames;
- the rest in polish, exact and refit.

An iteration is a Jacobian (2 evaluations per non-linear column, central) plus about 1.2 trial steps. Every refinement also ended with a covariance: 1 + 2 evaluations per non-linear parameter, about 10 % of a brief.

**(1) No intermediate covariance.** The covariance is made after convergence, and only the returned fit's is read. Dropping it cannot change any step: 0.908× the evaluations and identical minima on 22/22 runs.

**(2) Forward differences.** They halve each Jacobian.
- The iteration counts did not change at the median (brief 7.9; full 11.4 against 11.5), and the minima were today's on 22/22 runs.
- Where the path diverged, the fit ended at the same χ² (cylinder-P4mmm-on: 45 against 32 full iterations).
- The ratio by class is 0.49–0.58. It is highest in 4/mmm and m−3, where trial steps and audits weigh more in a run.

**Why wall time falls less than evaluations.** 96–98 % of the search's time is in pattern evaluations. An evaluation outside a Jacobian (trial step, FCJ audit, covariance) costs 1.5–2.5× a Jacobian column. Forward differences halve only the cheap Jacobian evaluations, so the dear ones become a larger share: 16 % → 27 % on box-Pm-3-near, 6 % → 12 % on ellcyl-P2m-generic. At today's costs this mix alone raises the mean cost per evaluation by 5–8 %, which accounts for 5–8 of the 12 % by which fwd's paired wall ratio (0.593×) exceeds its evaluation ratio (0.527×). The measured rise over five profile pairs is 4.5–23 %, and the same search's time varied by 16 % between two profile runs, so the remainder is within load noise. The higher cost outside the Jacobians is inferred to come from caches the engine keeps when only one parameter moves; this was not traced.

**The central pass.** On a forward-difference minimum it costs 1 iteration (44 evaluations median) and moves χ² by 0.0003 χ²_ν median: the forward and central minima are the same point. Its few moves (at most 0.61 χ²_ν, 4.5 % in an extent, 1.7° in an axis) are all free fits in flat valleys, where the shift test had stopped. Its marginal cost over the covariance it replaces is 24 evaluations a run.

**(3) Held frames.**
- The refinement is equivariant under the class's rotations, so equivalent frames end at the same χ² in the same number of evaluations, and skipping them changes nothing.
- They exist only where a rotation of the class maps one candidate frame onto another, which is in the eight classes with a 3-, 4- or 6-fold axis: 6/mmm 6, −3m 5, m−3 5, m−3m 4, 4/m 3, 4/mmm 3, −3 2, 6/m 1. That is 29 of 124 held refinements on the 77 runs, and none in −1, 2/m or mmm.
- The held refinements are a small stage, so the saving is small: 28 evaluations a run.

**(4) Symmetry and starts.**
- lowIndexAxes already gives one axis per Laue family, and a plate and a needle along one family are different starts, so no deterministic start is equivalent to another.
- The only symmetry redundancy is the random fill to 11. It exists only where the class has fewer than 5 low-index families: 2 random starts in −3m, 6/m and 6/mmm, and 4 in cubic. That is how higher symmetry already lowers the number of distinct starts.
- Dropping the fill saves 15 % of the search in those five classes, which then run at 36–49 % of today's evaluations. With the turns held fixed it costs nothing measurable: the same best χ² as fwd in 33/35 runs (the other two ±0.3 χ²_ν), and the same reach (25/27), outcomes (35/35) and solids.
- Restricting the fill to the fundamental zone, at 20° from every start, reaches less (9/10 against 10/10) and costs more than dropping the fill (0.489× against 0.441×). A uniform random rotation is already uniform in the zone modulo symmetry, and the deterministic starts reach the fill's basins anyway.

**The random turn is a noise source of its own.** A 0.02 rad turn about a random axis precedes each polish and the refit. In flat valleys it alone decides which free minimum is returned. On cylinder-Pm-3m-on, every method refines from the same held fit (16949.54), and the refit ends at 16943.18–16955.81 depending only on the turn: up to 7.5 χ²_ν of the best fit. Shifting the stream changed cost by up to 29 % in a run (box-P6m-generic) and moved a sphere kept as a box by about 1–2 % and 1–3°. Comparisons between start modes are therefore like-for-like only with the turns held fixed, as they now are.

**(4b) Full refinements from distinct brief ends.** The 3 best brief ends are often duplicates by an 8°/28 % test (52 of 77 runs). Dropping the duplicates looks safe on the pilot logs (69 of 78 ended alike) but costs reach on the 77, up to 191 χ²_ν on box-Pmmm-on. Briefs of 8 iterations are not converged, and ends that close can still lead to different minima.

(b) The reach bullet now uses bestC (the returned fit): 54/63 within 0.1 χ²_ν, 6 lower, box-Pmmm-on +1.81. score.mjs now prints this comparison for every variant, so it no longer comes from a separate reading. tried.name: ib: (a) the breadth convention alone
tried.idea: A Lorentzian whose integral breadth is 1/<L>_V: the FWHM is scaled by 2/(pi*0.675) = 0.943.
tried.results: Line alone: 17.0 % of the peak (18.3 %); <L>_V read / true 1.097. Pattern: 11.7 % (15.3 %); excess chi2_nu 0.66. Truth reference on the 22 sub-screen rows (sub-all.md): thinnest +15 % (lor +22 %); worst +31 % (+68 %), the same as lor; axis 4.2 deg (lor 5.5); chi2_nu 1.43, the same as lor. Clean anisotropy 0.82, the same as lor; 0.13 in m-3m. Cost: the same as lor.
tried.verdict: Dropped after the truth reference. It only rescales the size: about 6 points of the uniform over-read go, but the line's shape, the equant pull and the misfit stay.

tried.name: mom: (b1) TCH line matched by moments
tried.idea: Per member, the engine's TCH pseudo-Voigt with Gaussian and Lorentzian widths (g, l) chosen so that it has the exact line's integral breadth and Porod tail. The widths come from tables in the reduced shape along the member, built by this folder's own Fourier transform of A(L).
tried.results: Line alone: 5.4 % of the peak (6.9 %); <L>_V read / true 1.042. Pattern: 4.2 % (6.0 %); excess chi2_nu 0.10. Truth reference on the 22 sub-screen rows: thinnest +3 %, middle -4 %, longest -7 %, worst +15 % (+36 %), axis 3.1 deg, chi2_nu 1.08. Clean anisotropy 0.87. Cost: as lor (bench 3.7-8.3 ms an evaluation against lor's 4.0-7.6).
tried.verdict: Dropped in favour of lsq. Matching the tail leaves the core too wide, so the long extents read short, and it is a little worse than lsq on every figure.

tried.name: lsq: (b2) TCH line fitted to the exact line, from tables (finalist)
tried.idea: Per member, the TCH (g, l) that best fits this folder's own exact line by weighted least squares, looked up by the reduced shape along the member. The ball family (sphere, ellipsoid, spheroid) has one entry. Cylinder and elliptic cylinder use the angle psi from the axis in the scaled body, 0-90 deg by 0.5 deg, linear. The box uses the two ratios beta, gamma of the sorted scaled direction components, 0-1 by 0.025, bilinear. The values feed the engine's own TCH line, and the isotropic sphere's line goes through the same tables. Building the tables takes 18 s. This folder's A(L) agrees with the generator's to 3e-15 of the peak, but the model never calls the generator.
tried.results: Line alone: 4.5 % of the peak (6.4 %); <L>_V read / true 1.000 (1.000-1.000). Pattern: 3.6 % (5.6 %); excess chi2_nu 0.04 (90th 0.12; at most 2.8, on a size-distribution row). 77-run set, truth reference: thinnest +1 %, worst +13 % (+338 %), axis 3.1 deg, chi2_nu 1.06. Clean rows: worst +9 % (+42 %), anisotropy 0.95. Today's search: 65/66 kept, reach 65/66, worst +16 % (+232 %), thinnest +1 %, axis 4.3 deg (31.8). Clean: worst +10 %, axis 3.8 deg, anisotropy 0.95 (0.72-1.19). By solid, worst extent: box +21 %, square box +17 %, cylinder +8 %, ellipsoid +17 %, spheroid +10 %, elliptic cylinder +199 % (its height is put on another extent). The one miss is ellcyl-P6mmm-on (delta 807 chi2_nu; lor also missed it, at 62.9). Spheres: 2/11 kept, sphere-P6mmm-1 (texture, dBIC -365) and sphere-Pm-3m-3 (size distribution, -1775). The two small clean spheres that lor kept are now rejected early (dBIC +326 and +1539). Cost: 99 s a run, 3552 search evaluations, 14.1 ms an evaluation; 127 min for the set. Under one load (bench-*.json) lsq costs 3.4-8.1 ms an evaluation against lor's 4.0-7.6.
tried.verdict: Adopt as the default line: same cost as today and most of the bias gone. What it leaves: its own error of 2.5-8 % of the peak, the same size as the differences between solids' lines, so near-equant or high-count solids are still chosen with a bias (see the solids).

tried.name: wppm: (c) the exact line by the Fourier route (finalist)
tried.idea: The engine's own WPPM profile (FS2A_PROFILE=wppm): each member's line is the transform of the solid's analytic A(L) (engine xrd-broad covBase) multiplied by the instrument and strain, drawn by the engine's wppmLine. Caveat: the generator draws its correction term with the same wppmLine FFT and the same analytic formulas in separate code (gen/kernels.mjs). So (c) agrees with the data partly by construction (an inverse-crime risk). Read it as the ceiling for an exact model.
tried.results: Pattern: 0.29 % of the peak (0.65 %); excess chi2_nu 0.000 (at most 0.04 without the size-distribution rows), the TCH's own error in the generator's main term. 77-run set, truth reference: thinnest +0 %, worst +4 % (+410 %), axis 1.3 deg, chi2_nu 1.01. Clean rows: worst +2 % (+26 %), axis 0.7 deg, anisotropy 0.99 (0.96-1.10). Today's search: 66/66 kept, including the 6 truths lor rejected; reach 62/66, worst +4 % (+335 %), thinnest +0 %, axis 1.6 deg (14.4). Clean: thinnest +0 % (-1..+1), middle -0 % (-7..+3), longest -0 % (-4..+7), axis 0.9 deg (8.3), anisotropy 0.99. Per class on clean rows (search) the anisotropy is 0.92-1.09; for comparison, lor reads 0.11 in m-3m and 0.41 in 6/m, and lsq reads 0.88 and 0.96. By error kind, worst extent: hump +7 %, air +2 %, size distribution +16 %, impurity +19 %, texture +inf (3 of 6 rows unbounded). All 6 unbounded results are on error rows (texture 3, size distribution 2, impurity 1). Misses: sqbox-Pmmm-generic (clean, 6.6), cylinder-Pm-3m-on (size distribution, 1502), ellcyl-P-3m1-near (size distribution, 1.5), ellipsoid-Pm-3-on (texture, 216). Spheres: 2/11 kept, the same two as lsq (dBIC -327 and -3483). Cost: 254 s a run, 3331 search evaluations, 33.9 ms an evaluation; 325 min for the set, 2.2x lor. P-1 takes 953 s a run. Under one load (bench) an evaluation costs 12.4-78.6 ms, 2.4-13x lor's, growing with the member count.
tried.verdict: The most accurate model, at 2.2x today's time. It is needed to tell solids apart (see the solids). Model errors (size distribution, texture) are now read as shape more readily.

tried.name: hyb: lsq search, WPPM end
tried.idea: Today's search with the lsq line. Then up to 3 lowest distinct full ends, plus the isotropic fit, are refined again in WPPM. The keep criterion and the report are made in WPPM.
tried.results: Sub-screen (22 rows): worst +6 % (90th +334 %), thinnest +0 %, axis 2.8 deg (24.8). For comparison, wppm gives +6 % (+29 %) and 1.9 deg (14.9), lsq +16 % (+195 %) and 3.5 deg. Failures: ellcyl-P4mmm-generic +266 %, ellcyl-P6m-generic +2892 %, ellcyl-Pm-3m-generic +342 %, spheroid-P6mmm-near +243 % (axis across), cylinder-Pm-3m-on +inf. Spheres: 2/11 kept. Cost: 181 s a run, against wppm's 272 and lsq's 108 (sub-screen means).
tried.verdict: Dropped. The line used in the search decides the basin (the elliptic cylinder's height, an axis across), and a WPPM polish cannot leave it.

tried.name: inmodel: the floor (the engine's own lines in the data, lor model)
tried.idea: The truth reference when the data are drawn with the engine's own Lorentzian lines (--kernel none).
tried.results: Sub-screen clean rows: worst +9 % (+21 %), axis 1.9 deg. The exact model on exact lines (wppm) does better: +4 % (+10 %) and 0.9 deg.
tried.verdict: The exact lines carry information beyond <L>_V: their shape changes with direction, and the exact model reads it.

tried.name: the solids: cross-solid fits
tried.idea: Each of the 11 clean sub-screen rows searched as each of the six solids, with freeShape's early rejection off and the true solid's run copied from the sub-screen search. Each row is scored by chi2 and by BIC = chi2/chi2_nu,iso + P ln N. Counted as right, as a nested member of the truth's own family (box with square box, elliptic cylinder with cylinder, ellipsoid with spheroid), or as wrong (another family).
tried.results: Right / nested / wrong, by chi2 and then by BIC: lor 5/1/5 and 6/1/4; lsq 7/3/1 and 6/2/3; wppm 7/4/0 and 7/3/1. The lor errors pick a different family: box-P-1 as elliptic cylinder; ellipsoid-Pmmm as box, worse than the true ellipsoid by 31 chi2_nu; cylinder-P4mmm as box, by 70; ellcyl-Pm-3m as square box. The lsq errors: cylinder-P6m-on as spheroid by 7.2, and by BIC box-P-3m1 and ellcyl-P6m as spheroid; at 21 916 counts cylinder-P4mmm-on is fitted better as elliptic cylinder by 126 chi2_nu. The wppm misses are nested choices: ellipsoid 5.2x20.1x21.1 read as spheroid; ellcyl 44.8x58.5x9.8 and 17.0x52.1x6.7 read as cylinder. Its one cross-family miss is box-P-3m1-near read as cylinder by BIC, at 906 counts with 2.1 chi2_nu between them. Cost a search: lor 65 s, lsq 60 s, wppm 187 s.
tried.verdict: Only the exact line tells the families apart (11/11 by chi2, 10/11 by BIC). Within a family, BIC chooses the simpler member unless the data support the extra ratio.

tried.name: what sets the solids apart: colmatch, colsep, linediff, the family test
tried.idea: Four checks. (1) colmatch: each candidate's best match of the truth's <L>_V over the measured members, as the rms of ln<L>_V; within a reflection only the multiset counts. (2) colsep: the noise-free in-model separation, with the engine's own lines at the row's counts. (3) linediff: the exact lines of different solids at one <L>_V. (4) family.mjs: a family of two members with <L>_V of 1 +/- delta, fitted by one line model.
tried.results: Column lengths: the families of different shape separate at an rms of 12-25 % (in-model 240-2800 chi2). Nested pairs sit at 0.0 %. Different families can come close (box vs elliptic cylinder 1.1-1.7 %; ellipsoid vs spheroid or box 0.8-2.6 %). These near pairs give only 0.1-16 chi2 noise-free in-model, for example spheroid-P-3-near 0.1, box-P-3m1 0.5, ellcyl-P6m 0.2. With exact lines wppm separates the same pairs by 11-34 chi2_nu where the lines differ (spheroid-P-3-near: box 30, square box 34, cylinder 13, elliptic cylinder 11; box-P-1 vs elliptic cylinder 26; ellcyl-P2m vs box 32), but not at 906 counts (box-P-3m1: 1.6-3.3) or for a thick plate of wide extents (ellcyl-P6m vs box: 0.3). Linediff: lines differ by 1-12 % of the peak. Distinct <L>_V: 34-42 of 61-73 members at generic or low symmetry, 8-13 for on-lattice tetragonal, hexagonal and cubic truths. Family test: lor reads zero spread up to delta 0.5; lsq reads 0 at delta 0.1, 0.48 at 0.2, 0.90 at 0.3 and 1.0 at 0.5.
tried.verdict: Explains the confusion and the equant pull (see why). One run (colsep with exact lines and wppm) failed before its weights fix; its output is kept as colsep-exact-wppm.broken.out, and it was not rerun because the noisy cross-solid fits give the same separations.

result.why:
**1. Why the Lorentzian is biased.** At one <L>_V the Lorentzian is 11.5-21 % of the peak off every solid's exact line (linediff.md). Fitted alone it reads <L>_V 16 % long: 6 points of that are the breadth convention, the rest is the shape.

**2. Why it pulls solids toward equant, more the higher the symmetry.** The members of one reflection sit at one 2θ, so their lines add. In a high-symmetry class a reflection carries many members (m-3m: 10 reflections, 73 members; -1: 70 and 70), and the solid's anisotropy shows only as the spread of widths inside a family, that is, in the summed line's shape. On-lattice tetragonal, hexagonal and cubic truths have only 8-13 distinct <L>_V values; generic or low-symmetry ones have 34-42.
- A sum of lines of different widths is more Lorentzian-like than one line, and the Lorentzian is already too Lorentzian for the exact line. The fit therefore collapses the spread: the family test reads zero spread for δ up to 0.5.
- lsq still loses small spreads: it reads none at δ 0.1 and half at δ 0.2.
- WPPM reads them, so its anisotropy is about 1 in every class. Clean search: lor 0.11 in m-3m and 0.41 in 6/m; lsq 0.88 and 0.96; wppm 0.92 and 1.06.

**3. Why solids are confused.** There are three cases.
- **Nested families** (box and square box, elliptic cylinder and cylinder, ellipsoid and spheroid) have the same column lengths in the special case (0.0 %). χ² always prefers the general solid; BIC prefers the simple one unless the data support the extra ratio. These are statements about a ratio, not wrong solids.
- **Different families with near-equal column lengths.** Box against elliptic cylinder comes within 1.1-1.7 % rms of ln<L>_V; near-equant bodies come within 0.8-2.6 %. Lines that read only <L>_V give such pairs 0.1-16 χ² noise-free at 900-18 000 counts, so they cannot be told apart. Only the lines' shapes can: the exact lines of different solids differ by 1-12 % of the peak (ball against a box edge 4.8 %, ball against a cylinder across 1.7 %, box body diagonal against edge 12.4 %; a box along an edge and a cylinder along its axis are the same line). With the exact model these pairs separate by 11-34 χ²/χ²_ν.
- **A line model whose own error is larger than those differences** cannot tell the pairs apart, and its misfit is absorbed by whichever solid's spread of widths inside a family imitates it best. That is how lor chooses box for an ellipsoid (by 31 χ²/χ²_ν) and box for a near-equant cylinder (by 70). lsq's 2.5-8 % error is the same size as the differences, so it gets most families right but is biased in near-equant and high-count cases: the cylinder 5.7×5.7×6.4 at 949 counts goes to spheroid by 7.2, and at 21 916 counts the cylinder is fitted better as an elliptic cylinder by 126 χ²/χ²_ν. The number of measured directions bounds what column lengths can say, so high symmetry leans on the line shape more.

**4. What remains unresolved with the exact line.**
- Low counts: box-P-3m1-near at 906 counts, with 1.6-3.3 χ²/χ²_ν between families.
- Wide extents whose lines approach the instrument's width: the 45×58×10 nm plate, 0.3 between box and elliptic cylinder.

**5. Why the hybrid fails.** The basin is chosen by the line used in the search: the elliptic cylinder's height, or the spheroid's axis across. A WPPM polish of lsq's ends cannot move it.

**6. Why model errors leak into the shape.** With exact lines, a family's spread of widths imitates a size distribution, and texture re-weights members, so a free shape absorbs both: the 6 unbounded results and the size-distribution sphere kept as a spheroid.

**What would fix the remaining confusion:**
- the exact line in the search, not only at its end;
- a reported answer per nested family: the family, plus whether its extra ratio is supported;
- an explicit "family not determined" result when the families lie within ΔBIC 10;
- a size distribution and texture in the model (the engine's WPPM already carries a lognormal σ), with the per-line χ²_ν flag and jackknife the protocol plans.
open: Making WPPM cheaper is the next lever. It costs 2.2x a run and 2.4-13x an evaluation, and P-1 runs 953 s. Untested options: lsq only for the search's brief trials, with WPPM for every full refinement and every comparison (so the basin is chosen in WPPM, unlike the hybrid); fewer Fourier nodes; cached per-member transforms.

A better few-parameter line than TCH (for example two pseudo-Voigts per member, or a third shape parameter in the tables) could close lsq's gap at today's cost. Today lsq's 2.5-8 % error matters at high counts (cylinder-P4mmm-on truth reference chi2_nu 3.02 against 1.00 with WPPM) and in near-equant solids. Not tried.

Inverse-crime caveat for (c): the WPPM model and the generator's correction term share the engine's wppmLine FFT, and both use the same analytic A(L) formulas (written separately in engine covBase and gen/kernels.mjs). Its 0.29 %-of-peak agreement is partly by construction. Not run: an independent check of the engine's WPPM member line against this folder's own Fourier lines (lines/profiles.mjs). The (b) tables are this folder's own and were checked against the generator's A(L) to 3e-15.

Model errors with exact lines. WPPM leaves 6 extents unbounded, all on error rows (texture 3, size distribution 2, impurity 1), and keeps the 4.4 nm size-distribution sphere as a spheroid (dBIC -3483; lsq -1775). This needs a refined size distribution sigma (the engine's WPPM has a lognormal), texture, and the protocol's per-line chi2_nu flag and jackknife.

Reporting rule for nested families (box/square box, elliptic cylinder/cylinder, ellipsoid/spheroid): the family, plus whether the extra ratio is supported (BIC within the family). Also an explicit 'family not determined' outcome when the families lie within dBIC 10 (box-P-3m1-near at 906 counts; wide plates).

The confusion matrices rest on 11 clean sub-screen rows, one or three per solid. The protocol's confirmation on the 154 tuning runs should repeat the cross-solid fits with the adopted model, including error rows.

Reach is judged against each model's own truth reference: lsq 65/66 and WPPM 62/66 are not on one chi2 scale. The lsq miss ellcyl-P6mmm-on (delta 807; lor also missed it, at 62.9) is a basin that the WPPM search finds exactly (0 %, 0 deg).

Wall times are not like for like. lor ran in the pilot on 3 processes; lsq and WPPM ran here on 2, beside track B's 2. Search evaluations, and the bench run back to back under one load, are the fair cost comparison.
Track B's efficiency steps (no intermediate covariance, forward differences, frame dedupe, symmetry-cut starts) were measured on lor and must be re-checked on lsq and WPPM.
colsep with exact lines and WPPM (the noise-free separations) failed before its weights fix and was not rerun. The noisy cross-solid fits stand in for it.
